title: Brand name testing: how to test names before you commit
summary: A step-by-step framework for brand name testing that reveals the associations behind a name, not just which one people prefer.
body_markdown:
How does brand name testing online work? +


Online brand name testing now means asynchronous, AI-moderated interviews that probe associations and category fit, rather than a digital brand name testing survey. Participants react to each name on video, and the AI research assistant follows up on what they say. That adaptive probing turns a vague reaction like "interesting" into specific evidence about credibility and purchase intent, something static survey respondents never get.


What is the best brand name testing approach? +


The best brand name testing approach pairs preference ranking with structured qualitative probing into associations, category fit, and distinctiveness, all from the same participants. First, show each name as a single stimulus to capture honest first impressions. Participants then describe what each name suggests about the offering, audience, and price tier. The session closes with multiple stimuli side by side, asking which name participants would launch and what risk the weakest option carries.


How many names should you test at once? +


Test three or four names per brand name testing session. Beyond that, fatigue sets in, and order effects favor whichever name appeared first. Split larger shortlists into separate cells so the data stays comparable.


Does brand name testing work for global launches? +


Yes, brand name testing works for global launches, provided each market gets its own participants and category baseline. The AI research assistant works in 50+ languages and shows stimuli in each participant's language. Recruitment runs through 8 integrated panel providers plus your own participant lists, so a team can field the same shortlist in every market at once. Local category language is the critical variable. A name that reads as premium in one market can sound clinical or prove hard to pronounce in another, and only participants from each target market can identify which.


How is brand name testing different from a focus group? +


A focus group, the classic market research format, gathers group feedback in real time, which is useful when the team wants to hear debate. AI-moderated interviews are a key \[alternative to focus groups\](/insights/alternatives-to-focus-groups): each participant can provide feedback without hearing anyone else first, so group influence doesn't shape the initial read. Many naming teams use both, choosing based on what the decision needs.
